title: Customer service operations: The operating model behind high-performing B2B teams
summary: Learn how customer service operations help B2B teams manage workflows, SLAs, and customer communication at scale without losing visibility or control.
body_text: Learn how customer service operations help B2B teams manage workflows, SLAs, and customer communication at scale without losing visibility or control. B2B customer service operations are fundamentally a coordination problem. According to Front’s Coordination Tax report , B2B companies spend nearly three hours coordinating for every one hour spent solving customer problems. As customer work moves across teams, systems, and channels, the question isn’t whether you have the right people; it’s whether the system around them is built to keep contacts and ownership intact. This article covers what effective customer service operations look like in B2B, where complexity tends to break them, and how high-performing teams build the processes that hold up at scale. What are support operations in B2B customer service? B2B customer service operations are the workflows, systems, and accountability structures that help teams handle complex customer work — consistently, at volume, across multiple stakeholders. They typically include the following. Workflow and queue management Effective operations start with how incoming work gets handled. As customer requests arrive across email, live chat, and Slack, teams need clear processes for prioritization, routing, and load balancing. That means defining escalation paths and handoff workflows so that requests move to the right person without losing momentum or context. Cross-functional coordination In B2B customer service , most customer work doesn’t stay in one team. A billing and grief hold in finance. A compliance question routes to legal. A product issue involves engineering. Good customer operations management defines ownership at every stage and tracks issues through to resolution, so handoffs don’t become black holes. SLA and performance management Service-level agreements (SLAs) hold teams accountable and make performance measurable. Common SLA targets include: first response time, first contact resolution, overall resolution times, and escalation paths and timelines. Meeting them consistently requires organized workflows, balanced workloads, and clear accountability. Reporting and operational visibility Operations teams use customer service analytics to diagnose problems and improve processes. Beyond ticket volume, metrics that matter are workflow bottlenecks, coordination failures, recurring escalation patterns, workload spikes, and inefficient handoffs. With that visibility, you can fix systemic issues before they compound and gain the insights needed for more efficient customer support processes. Why do customer service operations become complex in B2B environments? Complexity in B2B isn’t a sign that something’s broken; it’s the baseline. Here’s what drives customer service challenges for B2B support staff. 1. Customer requests move across multiple teams Unlike B2C, where interactions are typically self-contained, B2B support requires coordination among multiple internal stakeholders. When requests cross people and channels without a shared system, context fragments. That’s when delays and inconsistency start. 2. Conversations happen across disconnected systems Without a unified customer service platform , information lives in silos: a Slack thread here, an email chain there, a CRM note somewhere else. Teams end up communicating with customers using incomplete information, which breaks consistency and erodes trust. 3. Ownership changes throughout the lifecycle of a request B2B queries often pass through multiple stages and multiple owners. Each handoff creates a risk of delays, missed follow-ups, and unclear accountability. As teams grow without updating their workflows , those risks multiply. 4. High-volume environments increase coordination pressure AI and automation help teams manage volume, but only when the underlying processes are sound. Front’s Coordination Tax report found that 93% of companies surveyed use AI in customer operations — yet 71% experienced significant AI-related issues in just the past three months. AI tools and automated workflows help teams manage high ticket volumes, but only if they have the right operational foundation in place. How strong customer service operations improve business performance Well-run operations create better outcomes on both sides of the relationship: Faster resolution without context loss: Organized handoffs mean customers don’t repeat themselves, and support requests move through the system faster — without dropping critical details along the way. More predictable service performance: Strong operational workflows help teams meet SLA targets, balance workloads, and handle escalations consistently. Customers know what to expect. Reduced operational drag across teams: Clear ownership, defined escalation paths, and routing make inter-team handoffs cleaner. Less time gets spent on coordination and overhead, more on actual customer work. Stronger retention in high-touch B2B relationships: Reliable operations build the kind of trust that holds long-term accounts together. And with AI and customer data to identify problems early and offer proactive support to fix them before they affect customer satisfaction. The role of AI in customer service operations today AI has become a core component of how B2B teams manage operational load, but how you deploy it matters. It’s built for the cross-team complexity of B2B customer support, with clear controls over what gets automated and what stays with your team. Assist teams with complex issues AI assistants help agents find relevant information, summarize long threads, and draft responses, without removing human judgment from the equation. Front Copilot pulls customer context instantly and suggests appropriate responses. Your team reviews every suggestion before it goes out, keeping high-quality customer communication and accountability intact. Analyze service quality and operational performance AI tools can monitor every conversation for shifts in sentiment or satisfaction. Front Smart CSAT automatically analyzes each interaction for satisfaction signals, while Smart QA reviews team performance across every conversation and flags where improvement is needed. How leading B2B teams run customer service at scale Centralize conversations and customer context Use an omnichannel platform that gives teams a shared view across all channels. When a logistics manager emails about a delayed shipment that originally came in via Slack, the support team needs instant access to the full thread — not a fragmented history across three systems. Build workflows around ownership and accountability Accountability has to travel with the work. Create routing rules and escalation paths that ensure every request goes to the right person, and structure each handoff so context stays attached and ownership is always clear. Track operational signals continuously Real-time metrics reveal where the friction is building before it reaches the customer. A spike in escalations from a specific manufacturing account might signal an integration problem. With visibility, you can act before it becomes an SLA breach. Breaking Down Silos: The Power of Integrated Behavioral Health and Chronic Condition Management
summary: The healthcare landscape is marked by a complex web of specialized care, often leading to fragmented patient experiences. Siloed care, where each provider (especially physical and mental health) is treated as a separate entity, can hinder positive patient outcomes. Integrated behavioral health and chronic condition management offer a transformative approach, fostering a holistic view of the patient and driving improved health outcomes.
body_text: The healthcare landscape is marked by a complex web of specialized care, often leading to fragmented patient experiences. Siloed care, where each provider (especially physical and mental health) is treated as a separate entity, can hinder positive patient outcomes. This is particularly evident in the management of chronic conditions, where behavioral factors significantly impact treatment adherence and overall well-being. Integrated behavioral health and chronic condition management offer a transformative approach, fostering a holistic view of the patient and driving improved health outcomes. The Holistic Power of Collaborative Care At the heart of integrated care lies the simple concept of collaboration. By bringing together healthcare providers from various disciplines – primary care, mental health, and chronic disease management – a comprehensive understanding of the patient emerges. This collaborative approach allows for a more accurate assessment of a patient’s needs, leading to tailored treatment plans that address both physical and mental health concerns. For instance, a patient with diabetes and depression benefits from a care team that coordinates treatment for both conditions, recognizing how each impacts the other. Clinical Collaboration and Improved Outcomes Enhanced Communication : Collaborative care fosters open communication between healthcare providers, breaking down the barriers that typically separate different specialties. This interconnectedness ensures that care plans are cohesive and comprehensive, reducing the risk of conflicting treatments and improving patient adherence to prescribed regimens. ‍ Improved Patient Engagement : Patients are more likely to engage in their treatment plans when they perceive their care as coordinated and personalized. According to a study published in the Journal of General Internal Medicine , patients receiving integrated care reported higher satisfaction and better engagement compared to those in traditional care models. ‍ Better Health Outcomes : The integration of behavioral health with chronic condition management has been shown to improve health outcomes significantly. A meta-analysis published in JAMA Internal Medicine found that patients with comorbid chronic physical conditions and mental health disorders experienced greater improvements in both physical and mental health outcomes when treated in an integrated care model compared to usual care. ‍ Cost-Effectiveness : Integrated care not only improves health outcomes but also proves to be cost-effective. The Millbank Quarterly reported that integrated care models can reduce overall healthcare costs by decreasing hospital admissions, emergency department visits, and redundant testing. Recent Data Supporting Integrated Care Reduced Hospitalizations and Emergency Department Visits: Integrated care models have demonstrated significant improvements in healthcare utilization. A 2023 study published in Health Affairs revealed that patients participating in integrated care programs experienced a notable 20% reduction in hospitalizations and a 30% decrease in emergency department visits compared to those receiving traditional care. These findings underscore the effectiveness of a collaborative approach in preventing acute care needs and improving overall health outcomes. ‍ Enhanced Chronic Disease Management: Patients with complex conditions benefit greatly from integrated care. Research from the American Journal of Managed Care in 2022 emphasized the positive impact of integrated care on diabetes and depression management. Individuals receiving combined care for these conditions exhibited significantly lower HbA1c levels, a key indicator of blood sugar control, and improved depression scores compared to those receiving separate treatments. This highlights the importance of addressing both physical and mental health for optimal chronic disease management. ‍ Increased Provider Satisfaction: ‍ Beyond patient benefits, integrated care has a positive impact on healthcare providers. A 2022 survey published in Medical Care found that healthcare professionals working in integrated care settings reported higher job satisfaction. The collaborative environment and the opportunity to witness the positive outcomes of comprehensive care contribute to increased professional fulfillment. This suggests that integrated care not only improves patient health but also enhances the well-being of the healthcare workforce. ‍ In a healthcare system often characterized by poor-quality, high-cost, and fragmented care, integrated behavioral health and chronic condition management emerges as a beacon of holistic care. By breaking down silos and fostering collaboration among healthcare providers, this approach delivers substantial benefits for patients, providers, and the overall healthcare system. Reduced hospitalizations, improved chronic disease management, and enhanced patient and provider satisfaction are compelling evidence of the transformative power of integrated care. As healthcare continuously evolves, embracing integrated care is essential for achieving optimal health outcomes and building a more resilient and patient-centered system. The positive impact on both patients and providers underscores the value of moving towards a more integrated, collaborative model of care. This transformative approach promises not only to improve individual health outcomes but also to contribute to a healthier, more efficient healthcare system as a whole.

title: 5E Advanced Materials Signs Letter of Intent With Corning Incorporated
summary: 5E Advanced Materials Signs Letter of Intent With Corning Incorporated
body_text: View PDF of This Release HIGHLIGHTS ﻿ 5E signs Letter of Intent with Corning Inc. to supply boron specialty materials 5E to collaborate with Corning to develop and supply boron advanced materials Corning is a Fortune 300 company and one of the largest technical glass manufacturers in the world, supplying precision glass to some of the world’s most innovative and influential companies, including leading consumer electronics manufacturers LOI aligns with 5E’s strategy to become a global thought leader and supplier of boron specialty and advanced materials and partner with industry leaders HOUSTON, June 06, 2022 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — 5E Advanced Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: FEAM) (ASX: 5EA) (“5E,” “We,” “Our,” or the “Company”) has entered into a non-binding letter of intent (“LOI”) with Corning Incorporated (NYSE: GLW) (“Corning”) to supply boron specialty materials. Under the terms of the LOI, 5E and Corning will work towards a binding agreement for the supply of boron specialty and advanced materials, which are used in the manufacture of Corning’s products. 5E and Corning will also collaborate and share technical know-how for the purpose of developing and enhancing boron advanced materials. Corning is a Fortune 300 company that draws upon materials science expertise and manufacturing process leadership to transform industries. Corning is one of the largest technical glass manufacturers in the world, supplying precision glass to leading consumer electronics manufacturers. Corning’s other glass, ceramic, and optics solutions serve other global markets, including but not limited to, flat panel displays, life sciences, semiconductor equipment optics and consumables, aerospace and defense optics, and telecommunications components. Commenting on the LOI with Corning, President and CEO, Mr Henri Tausch noted: “ We look forward to working with Corning, an industry leader in the global technical glass markets and a trusted partner to many marque brands. Corning’s leadership in the markets it serves offers a strong end use for our boron specialty and advanced materials. We are also pleased to support Corning’s sustainability commitments, as they align well with our environmental light-touch extraction and processing methods. We intend to have a long-term partnership with Corning as we focus on continuous innovation as technologies evolve. Today’s announcement marks another key milestone for the Company as we have now secured an LOI with one of the largest technical glass manufacturers in the world. We continue to experience strong market dynamics as we progress towards target construction completion of our Small-Scale Boron Facility in calendar fourth quarter 2022. ” About 5E Advanced Materials, Inc. 5E Advanced Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: FEAM) (ASX: 5EA) is an exploration stage company focused on becoming a vertically integrated global leader and supplier of boron specialty and advanced materials, complemented by lithium production capabilities. Our mission is to become a supplier of these critical materials to industries addressing global decarbonization, food production, and domestic security. We anticipate boron and lithium products will target applications in the fields of electric transportation, clean energy infrastructure such as solar and wind power, fertilizers, and domestic security. Our business strategy and objectives are to develop capabilities ranging from upstream extraction and product sales of boric acid, lithium carbonate and potentially other co-products, to downstream boron advanced material processing and development. Our business is based on our large domestic boron and lithium resource, which is located in Southern California and designated as Critical Infrastructure by the Department of Homeland Security’s Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and we intend to leverage this asset once commercially operational to internally supply our proposed downstream advanced material development activities over time. title: Mitigating Insider Threats: How To Do It
summary: Discover effective strategies to protect your organization from insider threats. Learn prevention, detection, and response techniques for internal risks.
body_text: Insiders (employees or partners) can hurt your business, and this is more serious than it seems. A report by Cybersecurity Insiders reveals that the percentage of organizations experiencing insider attacks rose from 66% in 2019 to 76% in 2024. Meanwhile, a report by the Ponemon Institute and Proofpoint highlights that nearly half of these incidents, 44%, are due to displeased employees messing with the organization's systems, tools, or apps. What are Insider Threats? Insiders are current or former employees, third-party contractors, or business partners who misuse their access to harm an organization . External partners like contractors or vendors can also pose significant risks. These can take many forms: Malicious activity Negligent threats Opportunistic threats Accidental threats It is crucial to address potential insider threats through appropriate measures and best practices to protect businesses from both accidental and malicious insiders. Not all insiders act with malicious intent; some may unknowingly put the organization at risk due to oversight or lack of training. Malicious insiders use their access to benefit personally or harm the organization intentionally. Negligent insiders may unintentionally create vulnerabilities, like clicking on a phishing link that grants unauthorized access. Understanding the context of users’ actions helps you understand their intent and motivation. Insider Threats to Organizations Financial loss from insider threats can be huge, from stolen funds to costly investigations and lawsuits. Techreport indicates that "the average cost of an insider threat situation in 2022 was $15.38 million." The market value of a company can drop significantly due to insider threats, affecting investor perception and stock price. The operational disruption caused by insider threats can result in lower production capacity and lower product market share. Beyond financial loss, insider threats can result in loss of competitive advantage if proprietary information is leaked to competitors. Intellectual property theft by insiders can result in the loss of valuable innovations and legal battles over ownership. Also, insider threats can cause reputational damage, loss of customers, and fines for non-compliance. Overall, insider threats are big risks that can put an organization’s stability, profitability, and public trust at risk. How to Mitigate Insider Threats Organizations need a good insider threat mitigation program to protect against these threats. This program should be multi-layered, incorporating people, processes, and technology to manage insider threats and reduce exposure to potential risks. Developing an insider threat program is key to addressing insider threats and protecting confidential information and intellectual property. Below are three key strategies to mitigate insider threats: employee training and awareness programs, strict access controls, and data protection measures. These three combined form a solid defense against insider threats and enhance the overall security of the organization. Employee Training and Awareness Programs Continuous training helps employees recognize and respond to insider threats. A good insider threat program with training and awareness initiatives covers all employees from entry-level to executives. There are many ways to deliver this training: online courses, in-person seminars, and printed materials. Bite-sized training at regular intervals can reinforce learning about insider threats. Employees should know the organization’s data handling policies and security awareness protocols. Having clear communication channels for reporting insider threats can boost organizational awareness and response. Half of insider threats are from careless insiders, so effective employee training is key. Employees should know what data they can access and how it can be used to minimize risk. Interactive training for employees who exhibit anomalous behavior can reinforce data handling protocols. Employees aware of the risks and know how to report suspicious activities reduce the likelihood of accidental insider threats. Strict Access Controls Access controls are key to protecting sensitive information from insider threats. Organizations should identify their assets and access permissions to mitigate insider threats. Multi-factor authentication reduces the chance of credential compromise, only authorized persons can access critical data. Strong passwords and thorough access control are key to protecting information. Advanced technology tools are needed to monitor user activities and detect unusual behavior that may be insider threats. Tailored insider threat detection tools can respond to potential threats before they escalate. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) tools can prevent both malicious and accidental insider threats by enforcing data handling policies. DLP software can identify sensitive information and enforce data access. Look into any red flags on unusual access activity. Strict access controls and advanced monitoring tools reduce insider threats and protect sensitive information from unauthorized access. Data Protection Measures Data protection measures are key to preventing access to critical company data. Strong access controls and DLP software can block sensitive information from being shared outside the organization. These measures can protect intellectual property, customer data, and other sensitive data from being compromised by insiders. Implementing strict security policies and following data handling protocols boosts the overall security of the organization. Proactive data protection is part of an effective insider threat mitigation program and protects critical data from threats. Insider Threat Response Plan An insider threat response plan is critical to responding to and mitigating insider threats. An insider threat incident response plan should have steps for containment, investigation, and recovery. When an insider threat incident happens, quick action to investigate and contain the threat reduces damage. Forensic evidence can help in insider threat investigations by adding screen capture and metadata. Effective insider threat detection systems provide alerts and detailed reports to facilitate timely investigation and response. Actions that can be taken in response to an insider threat incident are to revoke access, suspend or terminate employment, and contact law enforcement. Security team collaboration is needed to correlate activities and alerts and determine the best course of action for insider threats. Security teams play a critical role in managing insider threats and enhancing incident investigation efficiency. They must navigate complexities due to insider threats, as these individuals already possess legitimate access and knowledge of sensitive data, making detection and prevention challenging. Legal consequences of insider threats include fines for non-compliance and the cost of litigation. Developing and maintaining an insider threat response plan is key to minimizing the impact of insider threats on the organization. Using Technology for Insider Threat Detection Insider threats can come from employees but also from external partners, contractors, and vendors with legitimate access. Technology is key to effective insider threat detection. Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) solutions aggregate and analyze security data to help detect insider threats in real-time. Entity behavior analytics (EBA) analyzes user activities and can flag anomalies that deviate from established patterns as potential risks. Tools that provide real-time visibility into user activities help insider threat detection. These technologies can identify insider threats before they escalate, a proactive approach to insider threat prevention and mitigation. Risky Users and Activities Identifying risky users is important because insiders with legitimate access make it harder to detect malicious activities. Identifying risky users is part of insider threat mitigation. The process involves monitoring the observable behaviors of individuals to detect potential threats. Having a baseline of user activities allows you to detect deviations that may be risks. Behavioral analysis is used to compare user activities against standard behavior to detect anomalies. Repeated access to restricted data can indicate a deliberate insider threat. Anomalies are compared to standard and expected behaviors. This includes user activities too. Monitoring for repeated access to restricted areas can be a sign of insider threat. Behavior patterns like unusual file access or conflict with coworkers can be a sign of insider threats. Identifying and monitoring risky users and activities allows organizations to proactively manage insider threat risks. Insider Threat Best Practices Regular access control and user behavior audits can help detect insider threats early. Having a culture of transparency within the organization encourages employees to report suspicious activity without fear. Security team and HR collaboration is key to insider threat management. Mature insider threat programs make the organization more resilient to disruptions. Insider threats can damage the organization’s professional reputation and often lead to a loss of customer trust and a decline in sales. Implementing best practices for insider threat management helps organizations maintain a strong security posture and protect from within. Insider Threat Management Solutions Proofpoint’s Insider Threat Management is a converged DLP and ITM solution that detects and prevents insider threats on the endpoint in real-time. Proofpoint provides real-time, contextual visibility into user activity to prevent users from exfiltrating data through multiple channels like USB, web uploads, cloud sync, and print. The Application Control module of Proofpoint limits processes on workstations, while Heimdal’s Privileged Access Management allows administrators to elevate user rights, revoke escalations, and support zero-trust executions. Proofpoint’s solutions are cloud-native, scalable and API-driven to meet privacy and compliance requirements. By using these advanced solutions, organizations can enhance their insider threat prevention and mitigation protect company data, and maintain a strong security posture. FAQs What are insider threats? Insider threats are individuals (employees or contractors) who use their access to company data or systems to harm the organization. Security measures must be in place to mitigate this risk. How do insider threats affect the organization? Insider threats can cause financial loss, damage to reputation, disruption to operations, and data breaches. Organizations must have robust security measures in place to mitigate these risks. How to mitigate insider threats? To mitigate insider threats, prioritize employee training and awareness programs, strict access controls, and robust data protection. These will be your proactive defense against risks. How can technology detect insider threats? Technology can detect insider threats through SIEM and entity behavior analytics which provides real-time visibility into user activity. This allows organizations to detect unusual behavior and respond to potential threats. What should be in an insider threat response plan? Your insider threat response plan should include containment, investigation, recovery procedures, revocation of access privileges, and protocols for contacting law enforcement. These are the essential components. Conclusion In summary, insider threats are a big risk to organizations, financial stability, competitive advantage, and reputation. Understanding the types of insider threats and their impact is key to developing effective mitigation strategies. Key to mitigating insider threats is employee training and awareness programs, strict access controls, and data protection. Having an insider threat response plan and using technology to detect is also part of a robust insider threat management program. By following best practices for insider threat management and using advanced solutions like Proofpoint’s Insider Threat Management, organizations can prevent and mitigate insider threats. Proactive protection against insider threats is key to organizational stability, profitability, and public trust.

body_text: Make your first anniversary extra special with a gift that celebrates your unique love story. Instead of a typical present, turn a cherished photo – from a fun photoshoot or a special moment from your first year – into a stunning work of art with Instapainting . It’s a sentimental keepsake that captures the joy of your first year together, becomes a cherished tradition you can build on, and shows your partner you put extra thought into their gift. Don’t have a recent photo? No worries, any picture that holds special meaning can be transformed. This anniversary, give the gift of art with Instapainting! This article sparks creative photoshoot ideas to capture the magic of your first year together. Whether you’re a romantic couple or an adventurous duo, a photoshoot is a perfect way to make memories that last a lifetime. Plus, you’ll get stunning photos to cherish! We’ll guide you through location selection, outfit ideas, and capturing those perfect moments for a truly unforgettable anniversary. Choosing The Perfect Theme For Your 1st Year Anniversary Photoshoot Selecting the perfect theme for your 1st year anniversary photoshoot enhances the significance of your celebration. It sets the tone and showcases your shared interests and journey together. Timeless and Classic Ideas You embrace elegance and simplicity when choosing a timeless and classic theme. Consider these ideas: Black and White Glamour: Capture the essence of timeless romance with a black and white photoshoot. This style emphasizes strong emotions and the enduring nature of your relationship. Vintage Love Affair: Dress in vintage outfits from the era you love most, perhaps the 1920s or 1950s, and use props that complement that time to transport yourselves back in history. Elegant Evening Out: Wear formal attire, such as a gown and a tuxedo, and choose a sophisticated location like a classy restaurant or a ballroom. This setting creates a backdrop of luxury and opulence. Fun and Playful Themes If you and your partner enjoy lighthearted moments, opt for a fun and playful theme. Here are a few to consider: Carnival Craze: Head to a local fair or carnival. The bright colors, games, and festive atmosphere can add a joyful and youthful vibe to your photos. Picnic in the Park: Have a relaxed day with a picnic setup, complete with a basket, blanket, and your favorite snacks. It’s perfect for candid shots and natural laughter. Adventure Bound: If you’re lovers of the outdoors , capture your adventurous spirit with a photo session while hiking, at the beach, or in a kayak. Each theme offers a unique way to reflect your personal story and the connection you share. By picking a theme that resonates with your relationship, you ensure that your anniversary photoshoot is not just a photo session, but a celebration of your love. Selecting The Ideal Location Once you’ve chosen a theme for your 1st year anniversary photoshoot, picking the perfect location becomes your next crucial step. The right setting not only enhances the look of your photos but also helps encapsulate the emotions and story of your relationship. Indoor Photography Locations Indoor locations offer control over lighting and ambiance, making them ideal if you’re looking for a more styled and elegant setup. Consider these popular options depending on the mood and theme you’re aiming for: Art Galleries or Museums : These spaces provide a sophisticated backdrop filled with artistic details. Historic Mansions or Hotels : Embrace a touch of luxury and grandeur with their ornate interiors and rich textures. Cozy Cafés or Bookstores : Perfect for capturing a laid-back, intimate vibe. These venues not only shield you from unpredictable weather but also add a unique character to your anniversary photos. Outdoor Scenery Options If you prefer a natural setting, outdoor locations can be spectacular with their inherent beauty: Botanical Gardens or Parks : Offer lush greenery and colorful blooms that bring vibrant, natural colors to your photos. Beaches or Lakesides : Ideal for romantic sunset shots and a calm, serene backdrop. Urban Settings : Street art or historic city blocks can add an edgy, vibrant feel to your photographs. By choosing a location that resonates with your theme, you’ll make sure your anniversary photoshoot is as personal and special as your relationship itself. Remember, the location sets the stage for your stories to unfold naturally and beautifully. What To Wear For Your Anniversary Photoshoot Choosing the right outfits for your anniversary photoshoot not only boosts confidence but also ensures that your photos look cohesive and beautiful. Your clothes should complement the location and theme you’ve previously selected. Coordinating Outfits Match Colors Subtly: Opt for colors that harmonize without matching exactly. For example, if you wear a soft blue dress, your partner can choose a tie or shirt in a darker shade of blue. Consider the Season: Embrace seasonal colors and fabrics. A velvet dress or a wool blazer fits wonderfully in fall or winter scenes, whereas lighter cotton or linen suits summer settings. Dress for the Theme: If your theme is retro, think about vintage-style dresses or classic suits. For a more casual look, coordinated denim can work wonderfully. Add Layers and Textures : Scarves, belts, and jackets not only add depth to your outfits but also allow you to adapt to changing weather conditions during the photoshoot. Choose Meaningful Props : Incorporate items that hold significance in your relationship like a book you both love or a vintage camera. Select Complementary Accessories : Opt for simple jewelry and elegant watches that add a touch of sophistication without overwhelming the outfits. By dressing appropriately and adding thoughtful touches with accessories and props, your anniversary photoshoot can capture the essence of your celebration beautifully. Capturing The Right Moments After selecting the perfect setting and coordinating your outfits, capturing the right moments during your first anniversary photoshoot is crucial. This session isn’t just about taking pictures; it’s about immortalizing your journey together in a meaningful way. Professional Photographer vs. DIY Choosing between hiring a professional photographer and opting for a DIY approach depends largely on your personal preferences and the desired quality of your photos. Professional Photographer Expertise : Professionals possess the technical skills and artistic insight to capture high-quality images that frame your story beautifully. Equipment : They use professional-grade cameras and editing software to ensure stunning results. Stress-free : With a professional, you don’t have to worry about setting up shots or managing equipment, letting you focus fully on each other. DIY Photoshoot Personal touch : A DIY shoot allows for spontaneous and intimate moments that can feel more personal and relaxed. Cost-effective : You’ll save money on photography fees, which might help if you’re on a tight budget. Flexibility : You can shoot anytime and redo shots as many times as you like without the pressure of a structured session. Essential Shots to Include To ensure your photoshoot captures the essence of your relationship, consider including these essential shots: Candid Laughter : Capture moments of genuine laughter and joy between you two, which can often be the most memorable. Close-Ups : Include close-up shots that focus on your faces or specific details like holding hands or the texture of a fabric. Silhouettes : Try some silhouette shots during sunset or in front of brightly lit backdrops for dramatic effect. Walk Together : Shots of you walking hand in hand, perhaps down a path or along the beach, add a dynamic element and convey a sense of your journey together. Remember, the best photoshoot is one that feels true to who you are as a couple. Whether you choose a professional photographer or a DIY approach, make sure it reflects your personality and love story. Wrapping Up Anniversary photos are all about capturing the real you as a couple. So have fun, pick a theme that speaks to your hearts (or grab your phone for a DIY session!), and let your love for each other shine through. These aren’t staged portraits ; they’re snapshots of your unique story, filled with genuine smiles and the magic of your connection. Here’s to celebrating your first year and creating memories that will bring you joy for years to come!

title: What Are Customer Service Workflows And How to Build The Best One?
summary: Want to build customer support workflows that drive higher levels of customer satisfaction? Read on to learn more.
body_text: Gone are the days when price was the only differentiating factor when customers weighed different solutions. Customer experience (CX) is the new revenue driver, and repeated positive experiences will lead a customer to make repeat purchases or advocate for your business. The customer experience management market is expected to grow from $19.34 billion in 2024 to $70.20 billion by 2032 , at a CAGR of 17.5%, according to Fortune Business Insights. This highlights the growing importance of CX in business strategies. Besides that, Gartner reports that 89% of businesses recognize CX as a key competitive battleground Statista reveals that 44.5% of organizations globally see CX as their main way to stand out Also, customers spend 140% more after great experiences compared to negative ones However, to ensure an excellent and seamless service process, you must build robust and productive customer service workflows to ensure your agents and CX teams are always equipped to win and retain customers. In this article, we discuss how you can proceed. What Are Customer Service Workflows? Customer service workflows refer to processes that help you achieve your customer support goals through a sequence of steps. They act as a pre-defined blueprint of steps that easily integrate into and support your customer service operations. The process eliminates the need to create new action steps for every customer interaction, enabling agents to be more productive and deliver faster and more effective query resolution. Consider the scenario of creating a standardized, high-quality onboarding experience for every customer. Now, instead of mapping out a new onboarding plan each time, you’d want to follow a consistent approach that is rooted in proven techniques, like this one: Customer signs up for your product The customer receives an automated welcome email/message Guided product tour with the onboarding team Schedule routine check-ins Celebrate customer-centric milestones Importance of Building Customer Service Workflows Improves efficiency Automated workflows promote efficiency in customer service operations by streamlining processes, saving agents valuable time and energy otherwise spent on repetitive manual tasks. According to Salesforce , workflow automation is a top priority for 95% of IT and engineering leaders. This is further iterated by the fact that 74% of IT leaders have saved 4 hours each week by implementing workflow automation. Builds accountability You can design the workflows to assign specific queries to specific agents automatically. This defines responsibility and ensures that every query gets an adequate resolution without requiring multiple follow-ups. A unified system with tighter integrations These workflows also streamline customer support operations by consolidating all your tools and solutions into a single unified platform. Seamless integrations across your tech stack allow agents to manage all customer interactions in one place. Agents can perform multiple tasks, such as making and receiving calls while accessing a complete history of the customer’s interactions with the support team-resulting in faster query resolution. Proactive response Customers always appreciate prompt and hassle-free solutions to their queries. A customer service workflow helps eliminate operational bottlenecks hindering smoother service delivery. Agents don’t need to spend hours trying to figure out what works best-they have ready-to-use, plug-and-play workflows that help them focus on delivering a high-quality response. Performance overview for agents and teams Dynamic reporting and analytics integrated into the workflows offer a comprehensive view of agent and team performance. This allows for assessing productivity levels, identifying areas where service quality can be enhanced, and implementing strategies for continuous improvement in customer service operations. Types of Customer Service Workflows Here are some of the most commonly used customer service workflow examples that might be helpful for your business: Issue resolution workflows These are crucial for retaining customers and improving customer service operations. Here’s what a customer service workflow diagram for issue resolution looks like: Issue resolution workflow starts with ticket generation when the customer raises a query Sorting and delegating issues to relevant agents/teams Solving issues and/or escalating to senior teams or other technical teams/experts Deliver the solution or lay out the next steps for customers to follow Schedule follow-up or communicate a timeline for follow-up for less critical issues Close the ticket on conclusion of the issue Send feedback forms to customers to evaluate the quality of support Chatbot workflows Chatbots are the ideal channel for round-the-clock support as they facilitate customer self-service experiences. Here’s what a customer support workflow diagram for chatbot operations looks like: The customer types something or opens the chat window The chatbot greets the customer and sends a menu with predetermined options/questions The customer picks an option from the menu to raise a query The chatbot accesses the knowledge base to respond to customer queries The customer makes a choice that triggers actions to resolve the issue Feedback is gathered from the customer Customer order workflows Customer order workflows are integral to the customer experience, particularly for e-commerce businesses. This workflow is automated from the purchase of the product to the final delivery/receipt of the product to the customer. This is what a customer service workflow diagram for customer order processes would look like: The customer places an order Order is initiated within the order management system Order confirmation is sent via email/SMS The warehouse team is notified about the order The tracking number is initiated to be shared with the customer Product is delivered Product feedback workflow is initiated Product feedback workflows It is essential to have a customer service workflow dedicated to product development and improvement. How is your product faring? Which features are in demand? Which features need an upgrade? Did the customer face any problems in using your product? Here’s a customer service workflow diagram illustrating how product feedback workflows are recorded: A product feedback form is sent to the customer, acknowledging their effort Feedback is routed to relevant channels or segments Necessary modifications are implemented into the product Final communication is sent to the customer about implementing the product feedback How to Build a Customer Service Workflow: A Step-By-Step Guide Here’s a step-wise strategy to create a customer service workflow for your customer-facing operations: Step 1: Create a simple diagram of your workflow Unlike the linear diagrams given above for common customer support workflow diagrams, most workflows are much more complex. Each step has multiple ‘if this, then that’ scenarios that need to be accounted for, and it involves the following steps: Review the current processes Get started by taking stock of your current workflows. Define each step and the conditions that should be met for the process to be complete. Spotting loopholes in your workflows early on helps retain customers and generate higher CSAT scores. Alternatively, poorly designed customer service processes are a recipe for disaster. They can result in long wait times, inadequate resolution, and even agent burnout-each of which points to customer churn. What are the decision points? Decision points refer to the locations within a workflow where a process branches out. We have already mapped out a few customer support workflows relevant to different scenarios. However, in practice, these workflows are more nuanced and dynamic, which is where decision points come in. Decision points are where the workflow branches out into if/then scenarios. Here, a ‘then’ action is automatically initiated depending on the 'if' condition. What are your constraints? Constraints within the customer service workflow processes refer to regulatory requirements and financial compliance based on service level agreements and time frames. Step 2: Determine who interacts with your workflow Multiple stakeholders are involved in completing every workflow. You must clearly define who will interact with queries at each step of the workflow. This typically involves customer-facing teams and front and back-office departments supporting customer service functions. When building your workflows, consider the following aspects: Clearly define stakeholders and their roles To go deeper, identify how each interacts with the customers. Whether the customer experience teams carry out onboarding calls or the tech team ensures quick turnaround on bugs and other tech issues, each individual is a vital workflow component. Without clearly identifying each contributor's role, your customer support machinery will become a directionless web of actions. The departments where process stakeholders work Cross-functional collaboration across departments is essential for smoother movement within a customer service workflow. Let other departments involved in the workflow know how to prioritize and enable the resolution of customer service requests. Step 3: Identify your data requirements Knowing what data will be required to drive these workflows is an equally important step. Within automated systems, the support team must know where all the essential data is stored and how it will be synchronized between different stakeholders and departments. How will data be connected? Define how the data handoff between various stakeholders and departments will take place. Consider the scenario where an existing customer wants to add more features to their package. The process must ensure that all the necessary data reaches the product or other relevant departments. What does your tech stack look like? The software you choose must be compatible with the tech stack other teams use to ensure an automated and error-free flow of information between different systems and departments. Step 4: Use workflow automation tools Integrate your workflows using automation tools. These tools enable users to create and customize workflows without switching between tabs and/or windows. With enterprise-grade security and integrations like Shopify and Salesforce, the platform streamlines communication and enhances customer experience. Step 5: Test and refine Finally, the efficacy of every workflow is tested using real scenarios. At this stage, you must be able to answer the following questions: Has the customer support workflow truly advanced you toward your customer support objectives and/or improved your support team’s efficiency? Optimize customer service workflows by A/B testing multiple variants. Compare performance under identical scenarios and conditions to identify the most effective version, ensuring continuous improvement and the best possible customer experience. Best Practices for Creating Customer Service Workflows Let’s take a look at some of the best practices you can implement to drive higher ROI with your customer service workflows: Opt for the right tech stack Don’t rely on your CRM or voice software for customer support communications. Deploy an integrated customer support platform to your customer support workflow processes. Consolidating all your important tools into a single interface will simplify the creation of new workflows. Embrace continuous improvement in customer service processes Given the ever-growing expectations of customers today, your customer support management should be able to stand the test of time. Conduct regular process audits and upgrade your customer service workflows to meet the needs of modern customers. Follow a customer-centric approach When building your customer support workflows, keep your customers front and center. Maintain a consistent, high-quality experience for them from the start and throughout their journey with your brand. title: Cram IB Chemistry in 1 Week (2025): Survival Guide
summary: IB Chemistry cramming in 7 days for 2025: a practical survival plan, daily checklist, practice strategy, and RevisionDojo tools to boost marks fast.
body_text: The week you stop negotiating with chemistry At some point in every IB student’s year, there’s a quiet moment where you do the math. Seven days. One syllabus. A brain that keeps replaying TikTok sounds instead of electron configurations. And there it is, in plain numbers: you need IB Chemistry to work now . This is not the romantic version of studying, the one with color-coded notes and a sunrise run. This is the survival week. The goal isn’t “learn everything.” The goal is: turn your next seven days into the highest mark-per-hour you’ve ever lived in IB Chemistry . You can do that. But only if you accept one rule: you’re not revising to feel prepared. You’re revising to perform. A student tries to learn IB Chemistry in 7 days while chaos increases Your 1-week IB Chemistry checklist (read this first) Use this as your north star whenever you feel lost. Pick your exam level (SL/HL) and identify your weakest 3 topics. Spend 30% of time learning , 70% practicing (questions + corrections). Build a formula-and-method “one-pager” you rewrite daily from memory. Do at least 2 timed mixed sets and 1 full mock in the week. Track mistakes by type: concept gap , data booklet misuse , units , working shown , command term . Use one central resource hub so you don’t waste hours hopping tabs: IB Chemistry Resources . RevisionDojo is built for this exact situation: you’re short on time, long on pressure, and you need a system that tells you what to do next. That’s why students lean on its Study Notes, Flashcards, Questionbank, AI Chat, Mock Exams, Predicted Papers, Grading tools, Coursework Library, and Tutors when the calendar gets loud. The 2025 IB Chemistry map (so you don’t cram the wrong thing) The 2025 structure is easiest to think of as two big stories: Structure: what matter is and how we model it Particulate nature of matter, nuclear atom, electron configurations, the mole, ideal gases Ionic, covalent, metallic bonding; then how models become materials Periodic table and organic functional groups (classification) Reactivity: why reactions happen and what controls them Energetics: enthalpy, energy cycles, fuels; plus entropy/spontaneity (HL) Amount, rate, and extent: stoichiometry, kinetics, equilibrium ideas Mechanisms: acid-base, redox, and organic pathways When you cram IB Chemistry , this map matters because it tells you what compounds into everything else. The mole and bonding are like grammar. If your grammar is weak, every sentence costs double. If you want a clean set of syllabus-aligned summaries to start from, keep IB Chemistry Notes 2025 open all week. The 7-day IB Chemistry cram plan (with realistic daily targets) This plan assumes you have school, other subjects, and a human need for sleep. If you have more time, stretch the blocks. If you have less time, keep the structure and compress the notes. Day 1: Build the machine (diagnose, don’t drift) Goal: Stop guessing. Start targeting. Skim the syllabus map and mark: green (ok), yellow (shaky), red (panic). Do a 30-45 minute mixed diagnostic from a question bank. Create a “Mistake Log” with 5 columns: topic, mistake type, correct method, why you missed it, what you’ll do next time. Best place to practice immediately: Questionbank , then use AI Chat to ask why the mark scheme wants that exact phrasing. Night task (15 minutes): Start your one-pager (constants, key equations, recurring steps). Day 2: Structure sprint (atomic, mole, bonding) Goal: Make basic questions automatic. Learn fast from notes, then immediately switch to questions. Prioritize: electron configuration logic, mole conversions, bonding models, intermolecular forces. For targeted practice, pick a structured slice like Structure 3 questionbank to train classification and reasoning. Rule: if you get a question wrong, don’t just read the solution. Rewrite the solution as if teaching it to a tired friend . Two students try to befriend the mole instead of using units Day 3: Reactivity foundations (enthalpy and energy cycles) Goal: Turn energetics into a repeatable method. Memorize the shape of common problems: calorimetry setup, Hess cycles, enthalpy definitions. Do short sets: 10 questions, correct, then 10 more. If you feel behind, don’t widen your scope. Narrow it: get 3 problem types perfect. IB Chemistry often rewards method consistency more than vague coverage. Day 4: Rate + equilibrium thinking (how fast, how far) Goal: Stop treating kinetics and equilibrium as separate chapters. Kinetics: rate graphs, order, half-life style reasoning (where applicable), factors, experiments. Equilibrium: Le Chatelier logic, K expressions, what changes Q vs K. A focused practice hub helps here: R2.2 How fast? questionbank . Night task: Update your one-pager from memory. Don’t copy. Retrieve. Day 5: HL boosts or your weakest red zones Goal: Spend today where marks are currently leaking. If you’re HL, entropy/spontaneity is a common time-sink. Keep it practical: Identify what each symbol means and which direction implies what. Practice interpreting rather than re-reading. If you’re SL, this day is still for your “red zones.” The fastest way to raise your IB Chemistry score is to fix recurring errors, not to skim new pages. If stoichiometry is your pain point, drill it directly: R2.1 How much? questionbank . Day 6: Mock exam day (the truth serum) Goal: Convert knowledge into exam performance. Sit one full timed mock (or at least a long mixed set). Mark it strictly. Then re-attempt the wrong questions 24 hours later. Use RevisionDojo’s Mock Exams and Grading tools mindset: you’re not collecting scores, you’re collecting feedback loops . If you want exam-like conditioning, add IB Chemistry Predicted Papers for realistic timing and topic spread. A laptop refuses bribes and demands working shown Day 7: Calm review + strategy (protect the points you already earned) Goal: Go into the exam steady, not fried. Re-do your top 15 mistake-log questions. Rewrite the one-pager one final time. Practice command-term discipline: “state” vs “explain” vs “deduce.” Pack your exam kit. Sleep. A surprisingly high percentage of IB Chemistry points are lost to rushed reading and messy working. Day 7 is about reducing preventable mistakes. How to cram IB Chemistry without fooling yourself Cramming fails when it becomes a performance for yourself: long hours, lots of highlighting, very little retrieval. Here’s the smarter pattern. Use the 3-pass rule for every topic Pass 1 (15-25 min): Read concise notes, define key terms, copy one worked example. Pass 2 (35-60 min): Do exam-style questions immediately. No “one more page” promises. Pass 3 (10-15 min): Write a micro-summary from memory and add to your mistake log. RevisionDojo’s Study Notes give you Pass 1 speed; Flashcards make Pass 3 automatic; the Questionbank forces Pass 2 honesty. Build “methods,” not memories In IB Chemistry , you can often survive with 10-15 reliable methods: unit conversions + significant figures discipline mole ratios and limiting reagent structure equilibrium change predictions (what affects K?) energetics setup and common traps organic identification patterns and reaction expectations If you want a deep long-term plan after this week, read The Ultimate Guide to IB Revision Planning in 2025 . For this week, keep it narrow. Mini section: what about the IB Chemistry IA in the middle of exam prep? Sometimes your brain is juggling exam revision and IA deadlines. If that’s you, do not let your IA become an emotional black hole. Use high-leverage support: If you’re still shaping your topic: IB Chemistry IA Ideas in 2025 . If you’re writing and unsure what the criteria want: Navigating the IB Chemistry IA . If you need exemplars to calibrate quality fast: IB Chemistry IA Examples . RevisionDojo’s Coursework Library and Grading tools matter here because they reduce ambiguity. Ambiguity is what steals time. Closing: your job isn’t to feel ready, it’s to be ready A week from now, you won’t remember every late-night panic. You’ll remember that you finally stopped trying to “cover IB Chemistry ” and started trying to score in IB Chemistry . If you want the cleanest path through this week, keep everything in one place: RevisionDojo for Study Notes , Flashcards , AI Chat , the Questionbank , Mock Exams , Predicted Papers , and Grading tools that show you exactly where marks are being lost. Then, if you need human help in the final stretch, use Tutors to turn confusion into a plan. Cram smart. Correct ruthlessly. Sleep like it counts. And when you open the paper, remember: you’re not hoping for easy questions. You’ve trained for the hard ones in IB Chemistry .

title: BCP: transactions in the mass consumption ecosystem grew more than 30% over the last year
summary: Lima, June 12, 2024.– Over the last year, the number of transactions in the mass consumption ecosystem that were made through BCP increased 34%. This
body_text: En el BCP actualmente más del 70% de este tipo de transacciones pasan por canales digitales. Lima, June 12, 2024.– Over the last year, the number of transactions in the mass consumption ecosystem that were made through BCP increased 34%. This evolution reflects ongoing growth in digital transactions, which today account for more than 70% of all transactions conducted at establishments linked with mass consumption (including payments through transfers, cards and Yape). Expansion over the period was attributable accelerated digital transformation in the private sector, which was driven by growing demand for fast and efficient payment solutions. «At BCP, we are committed to growing and modernizing the collections methods used by Peru’s corporate world. Growth of more than 30% in the number of transactions in the mass consumption ecosystem reflects a change in consumer preferences as well as heightened efforts by our corporate clients to adapt to an increasingly digital market. Our objective is to continue generating alliances with the main companies in the mass consumption industry to facilitate the use of digital channels to serve companies’ client and supplier networks, » , commented César Stuart, Head of Corporate Banking del BCP. BCP’s Mobile Banking application and Yape, Peru’s superapp, have become highly relevant collections venues for mass consumption companies. In 2022, transactions were made primarily through physical channels and digital channels represented only 45% of total transactions. By 2023, these channels accounted for 60% of total transactions and in the first quarter, the number rose to 73%. Through strategic alliances through the main companies in the corporate mass consumption world, including Arca Continental and others, BCP offered bodega owners digital solutions, specifically direct payments with a code generated by Yape, to facilitate payments to suppliers. “At Arca Continental in Perú , we seek to drive the development of bodega owners in Peru, who are important players in the national economy. Facilitating digital payments with Yape to more than 370 thousand clients throughout Peru represents a milestone in the drive to digitalize the mass consumption sector,” said Segundo Capristán, Head of Finance at Arca Continental in Perú. César Stuart at BCP added: “The main clients for mass consumption companies are bodegas, markets and corner pharmacies. We see opportunities to use digital solutions to spur growth and formalization in this traditional market.” Growth in transactions in the mass consumption sector is also aligned with BCP’s efforts to promote financial and digital inclusion throughout the country.

title: Understanding Average m2 Furniture Pricing Across Luxury Tiers
summary: In this article we will cover the average interior fit-out costs in 2024 per category such as cabinets, pantries and closets. Read about the break down of prices and discover the average costs.
body_text: In the world of interior design, both designers and clients must understand the full scope of the costs. However, the average m2 cost varies according to project specifications, market conditions, and other factors. When calculating the square meter pricing for furniture, a few pointers must be taken into consideration. We're breaking it down for you in this blog. ‍ ‍ ‍ What influences the costs? Material costs : This includes the type of wood, hardware like hinges and knobs, finishes, and any other materials needed. Labor costs : It is important to estimate the labor costs involved in building the furniture. It takes time to manufacture the furniture, as well as pay the wages and any other overhead costs associated with labor work. Design complexity : The more complex the design, the higher the cost because it requires more time and skills to produce. Overheads and profit margin : Overhead costs typically include rent, utilities, and administrative expenses. The profit margin operates to cover business expenses and generate a profit. ‍ ‍ Costs breakdown ‍ Permits Building permits can also be added to your costs. It is therefore important to take this into account in your project time table and budget. A building permit can range from €50 to €450 depending where you live. ‍ Materials Materials depend on the scale and which type of wood you want for your project. The lowest option and the most often used for budget friendly projects is MDF, costing as low as €100. High-end material wood such as mahogany, cherry or oak could cost upward to €5000 depending on the size. ‍ Labor Labor costs can vary widely depending on the complexity of your project and the size. For a simple project it could be around €35 to €100 per hour. However, more complex work can get up closer to €200 euros per hour to hire a specialist. ‍ Accessories Accessories include things like shoe racks, custom lighting or island unit. This can range from €45 to €2500. It all depends on the complexity and sizing of your project, the more minimalistic and smaller in size, the less it costs. ‍ ‍ ‍ Closets and Storage ‍ Basic tier: Basic closets are great for budget-friendly projects. Basic closets are usually built of cost-effective materials like Medium Density Fiberboard (MDF) or plywood for panels and shelves. The average cost for basic MDF closets also depends on the height of the closet. Reach-in closets are seen as the most budget-friendly custom closet. Common features of the basic tier closets are as followed: Simple design Standard sizes and finishes Limited customization options Basic shelving and hanging space Materials are plywood or MDF The cost range can go from €160 to €360 per m² for MDF closets and plywood based closets from €200 to €300 per m². To be more specific, a reach-in closet has the range in price from €500 to €1500 (with an average of 800 euro for 4m² closet.). A two-door wardrobe (200 cm x 170cm) has the average all-inclusive price of €1720 (approximately €320 per m² for 5.2m²). The costs can decrease based on the material used, complexity, type of doors, and accessories. Additional costs such as the installation and transportation can also drive up the total price. ‍ Basic Tier : €160 - €300 per m² (average €230 per m²) ‍ ‍ Mid range tier: Mid range closets have hardwood veneers for a more sophisticated look compared to MDF. What makes a mid range closet differ from the basic tier, is its increased durability and improvement in aesthetics. Most mid tier closets are standalone wardrobes, and are most frequently used when the house does not have enough space for a built-in closet. However, built-in closets can be seen in this category as well. The most common features for this tier are: Enhanced durability and aesthetics Semi-customizable designs Better quality finishes Improved shelving, hanging space, and accessories Hardwood veneers as material The cost range can get around €400 to €700 per m² for hardwood veneer closets. Even within the mid tier, there are two options. The lower mid range, which is standalone wardrobe with the average costs of €400 to €500 m². Upper mid range goes from €500 to €700 m² for a built-in closet. A detailed breakdown as an example: the standalone wardrobe (300 cm x 270 cm) for an all inclusive price €3450, (approximately €426 per m²). A custom sliding door closet can start from €1300 (approximately €433 per m² for 3m²) ‍ Mid Range Tier : €400 - €700 per m² (average €550 per m²) ‍ ‍ High-end tier: High-end closets are crafted from solid wood, offering unparalleled quality and luxury. These closets may feature premium wood species such as oak, walnut, or mahogany. The storage options are usually more like walk-in closets or the option to store shoes and bags along with clothing. Glass cabinets can also be provided with options in accessories. The following characteristics are often seen in the high-end closets category: Premium materials and craftsmanship Fully customizable designs High-end finishes and hardware Advanced storage solutions (drawer systems, lighting) Solid wood as materials (oak, walnut, mahogany) A luxury walk-in closet (300 cm x 270 cm) can cost around €5250 all-inclusive, this is around €650 per m² for 9.1m2. However, if there is need for a larger high-end walk-in closet, the costs all-inclusive can range up from €4000 to €10,000+. Having the average of €7000 for 10m² which is around €700 per m². ‍ High-End Tier : €800 - €1500 per m² (average €1150 per m²) ‍ ‍ ‍ Pantry ‍ Basic tier: Basic pantries prioritize functionality over aesthetics. The most affordable materials and standard shelving are being used. MDF is the most popular option for this tier, as it is commonly used for simple projects. Reach-in cabinets are the most frequently seen within this tier, convenient for small kitchens and spaces. Reach-in generally allows you to reach for your item. Another cabinet within this tier is the slide out pantry with sliding shelves and rotating doors, integrated into existing cabinetry to maximize storage. Ideal for compact places to save space. Some of the features are: Simple design and construction Standard sizes and finishes Limited customization options Basic shelving and storage space MDF or basic woods (plywood, veneer) as material The cost can range from €50 to €300 per m², however it can add up, when extra applications or accessories are added for example. For basic MDF cabinets, the costs can be around €150 to €200 per m². When it comes to basic wood cabinets made out of plywood or veneer, it can lead up to €200 to €300 per m². As an example, a simple storage cabinet made out of MDF of 1.6 m² can cost around €175. ‍ Basic Tier : €150 - €300 per m² (average €225 per m²) ‍ ‍ ‍ Mid range tier: Mid range pantries often include hardwood veneers. That is due to its better durability and aesthetics when compared to MDF. For mid-range pantries, it may include some custom features and improved organization. In this tier, corner cabinets and freestanding pantries are seen. The corner cabinets are great for maximizing the space in a kitchen and are integrated within the kitchen design. Freestanding pantries are versatile and can be moved around freely. This also fits great in homes with additional space. There is mainly mix shelving and are usually complete with matching floors, cabinets, and kitchen hardware. Some of the features are: Enhanced durability and aesthetics Semi-customizable designs Improved shelving, cabinets, and storage solutions Wood veneer or higher quality MDF as materials The cost for a mid range pantry can range from €400 to €800 per m². For MDF with wood veneer cabinets, the costs can be around €400 to €500 per m². When it comes to a high quality MDF or veneer pantry, it can lead up to €600 to €800 per m². The average cost for a small walk-in pantry, it can be just over €2,000 for 2.32 m², approx. €865 per m². ‍ Mid Range Tier : €400 - €800 per m² (average €600 per m²) ‍ ‍ High-end tier: This tier of pantry cabinets are frequently constructed of solid wood, which results in craftsmanship and luxurious storage options. This is mostly common with large walk-in pantries with high-end custom amenities such as countertops, backsplash, bar, wine fridge and extensive storage capabilities. This is ideally for family houses and those who buy items in bulk. Another type of pantry within this tier is the butler pantry. Butler pantries have an extra countertop and serves as an extension of the kitchen. Useful when in need of additional workspace and somewhere to store appliances. Some of the features are: Premium materials and craftsmanship Fully customizable designs High-end finishes and hardware Advanced storage solutions and additional features (e.g., sink, wine fridge) Solid wood as material The cost range per m² can get around €1,000 to €2,000 depending on which solid wood material is used. For example, the average large walk-in pantry can go from €2000 to €3500 all-inclusive, €215 to €377 per m². A butler pantry can range from €5,000 to €10,000 for 10m², approx. €538 to €1,076 per m² ‍ High-End Tier : €1,000 - €2,000 per m² (average €1,500 per m²) ‍ ‍ Kitchen cabinets ‍ Basic tier: Basic tier is usually applicable when the kitchen is ready to be freshened up to get a new look. A small make-over is needed or a small renovation, enough to make it look as new. In this tier, the only focus is on functionality with the basic shelves and drawers. Most basic tier kitchen cabinets have a laminated bench top and plastic as basis to decrease the costs of the kitchen cabinets costs. Focus on functionality Basic shelves and drawers Laminated bench top Plastic basis for reduced costs The cost range per square meter for basic kitchen cabinets can go around €1,000 to €1,500 depending on the specific materials and finishes used. For example, a small kitchen renovation focusing on basic functionality might cost between €3,000 to €4,500 for 3m², which is approximately €1,000 to €1,500 per m². These cabinets often include basic shelves and drawers, laminated benchtops, and plastic bases to reduce costs. ‍ Basic tier : €1,000 - €1,500 per m² (average €1,250 per m²) ‍ ‍ ‍ Mid range tier: In the mid range, it is commonly seen that other options are used that costs a bit more money and time. This could be a new kitchen top, kitchen doors and knobs. Veneer and wood with a marble look are usually used and seen as a good choice to still give that exquisite look. New kitchen top, doors, and knobs Veneer and wood with marble look Improved aesthetic appeal The cost range per m² for mid range kitchen cabinets can go around €1,500 to €2,000 depending on the choice of materials and finishes. For instance, a mid-sized kitchen with upgraded materials might cost between €4,500 to €6,000 for 3m², which is approximately €1,500 to €2,000 per m². These cabinets typically feature new kitchen tops, doors, knobs, and materials like veneer and marble-look wood for a more refined aesthetic appeal. ‍ Mid range tier : €1,500 - €2,000 per m² (average €1,750 per m²) ‍ ‍ High-end tier: High-end kitchen cabinets include drawers that can be opened with the push of your finger. Some lighting can be included and accessories to give the kitchen a more sophisticated and elegant look. High-end accessories such as golden hardware or integrated appliances can amplify budget costs into the luxury budget tier. A higher range kitchen cabinets are of high gloss finish. Drawers with push-to-open mechanism Integrated lighting and accessories High-end appliances Golden hardware High gloss finish The cost range per m² for high-end kitchen cabinets can go around €2,000 to €3,000 depending on the premium materials and advanced features used. For example, a luxury kitchen renovation with high-end features might cost between €6,000 to €9,000 for 3m², which is approximately €2,000 to €3,000 per m². These cabinets often include push-to-open drawers, integrated lighting and accessories, high-end appliances, golden hardware, and a high gloss finish. ‍ High end tier : €2,000 - €3,000 per m² (average €2,500 per m²) ‍ ‍ ‍ In Conclusion... The average price depends on the type, size, complexity of your project. This article gives you a bit of an indication on how much your project could cost. It is however important to note that there can be soft economy powers that can have an effect on the costs in the future.
